messages.author: f9aa37fc453f9f0e
messages.subject: Way to ignore variables
parts:
Is there a way to prevent variables from the parameters block from being reported in the output csv? I believe intermediate variables defined in the model block are ignored, but I think the model block isn't the place to define variables with constraints; I get the following message when I try 
vector<lower=0>[5] forgetVar;
 in the model block:
SYNTAX ERROR, MESSAGE(S) FROM PARSER: require unconstrained. found range constraint.

Basically, I'm more interested in the hierarchical priors, and there are many space-consuming parameters that depend on these that I'm not interested in.

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Way to ignore variables
parts:
On Thursday, July 30, 2015 at 1:49:30 PM UTC-4, William Beard wrote:
Is there a way to prevent variables from the parameters block from being reported in the output csv?

Not in CmdStan. In RStan, there is a pars argument that takes a character vector of parameter names and an include flag indicating whether to include or exclude the parameters named in pars from the output.
I believe intermediate variables defined in the model block are ignored, but I think the model block isn't the place to define variables with constraints

The model block does not permit constraints (so you will get that parser error) but moreover, your Stan program is likely miswritten if you were trying to do that.

Ben

parts: On Thursday, July 30, 2015 at 1:49:30 PM UTC-4, William Beard wrote:
Is there a way to prevent variables from the parameters block from being reported in the output csv?

It's a problem I run in to a fair bit but I haven't found a great solution to this.  I don't mind the parameters all being written to file since I _might_ want them but when I try to load the file into something (R) to analyze it ends up being a nuisance to load the whole file.  The closest I see for a convenient solution is something like csvkit (https://csvkit.readthedocs.org/en/0.9.1/cli.html) which makes it easier to subset by columns but last I tried it had trouble ignoring the metadata parts of the file.
